kf: Conventional systemics: **methotrexate** (weekly), ciclosporin, acitretin, azathioprine, mycophenolate; biologics target specific cytokines.
Psoriasis biologics: TNF-α (adalimumab), IL-17 (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab), IL-23 (guselkumab, risankizumab); eczema: dupilumab, tralokinumab, JAK inhibitors.
Methotrexate is **once weekly**: prescribing errors (daily dosing) are fatal; folic acid on another day; monitor FBC, LFT, U&E.
Screen before biologics: TB (IGRA), hepatitis B/C, HIV; avoid live vaccines.
Infection on immunosuppressants needs early review; record specialist drugs in the GP record.
myths: **"Biologics are just stronger steroids"**: they block one immune pathway, with different risks.
patho_lead: Systemic drugs and biologics **interrupt the immune circuits** that drive chronic skin inflammation.

mech.t: Dendritic cell IL-23 sustains Th17 cells that release IL-17, driving psoriasis.
mech.cap: The IL-23/Th17 axis targeted by psoriasis biologics.

mech.t: IL-4 and IL-13 drive atopic eczema; dupilumab blocks the IL-4 receptor α.
Many cytokine receptors signal through JAKs; oral JAK inhibitors block several at once.
Methotrexate inhibits folate pathways in rapidly dividing immune cells.
mech.cap: Methotrexate is taken once a week.

comp: Infection (including TB reactivation), cytopenias, liver toxicity, kidney toxicity (ciclosporin), conjunctivitis (dupilumab), thrombosis risk (JAK inhibitors).
prog: Most patients achieve major improvement; treatment is long-term.
